- YTXTube music player: a Song / Video switch at the top, as in YouTube Music. Song shows the cover, Video shows the video of the same track in its place, and the music goes on either way.
- A thumb down ("not for me") next to the heart: the song is left out of what plays next, of the queue and of the music home (and kept across restarts), the next song plays, and a second tap takes it back. Signed in, the dislike is sent to YouTube too.
- YTXTube Series and movies is a page of shelves, not a form: a big title, a line under it, a search box, then "Popular series" and "Popular movies" as rows of posters; a tap opens the seasons (or the film's download). The add-on and the size are behind one row. It is in the Library tab (and still in Saved).
- YTXTube queue: no more "Playing next" / "Added to queue" / "Up next" messages. In the music player a queue button (with the count) next to the menu opens the list to play, remove or clear; the track menu has Play next and Add to queue; the video player's queue works the same. Other messages are lifted above the navigation bar (they sat under the bottom of the screen).
- Pulse's old launcher icons (Windows 95, XP, 7, 10, 11) moved from Settings to Extra apps > icon settings ("Pulse's old icons").
- Lyrics editor follows the look (it was always black). Word times: the pass that gives the lyrics on the phone their word times runs once more after this update (a find is taken when three in five of the lines match, it was four in five), and a song with no find is looked up again after a day instead of three.
- YTXTube's picture-in-picture window has a headphones button (play on in the background, audio only, the window closes) next to play / pause and next. The phone's own gear in that window is the system's and cannot be removed.
- Packs ask once the first time they are wanted ("Download it now (5 MB)?", e.g. the gym pictures); a yes downloads by itself, a no leaves the Download button. Packs come from this app's own repository; when GitHub does not answer, jsDelivr is tried (and the other way round).
- Word-by-word lyrics are everywhere the lyrics are: the lock screen window and the floating lyrics (the words sung in white, the rest dimmer) and the lyrics notification (the words sung in bold letters, the rest plain) fill as the line is sung.
- The packs under 1 MB (icons of the older looks, more XP and Windows 10 wallpapers, the Office Assistants: 8 of them) are one pack, "small" (2.2 MB), that comes once by itself the first time Pulse starts; each is still used by its own name.
- YTXTube music player: the video is not decoded any more while the cover is shown (the Song / Video switch turns it on), which is what made the music lag.
- One folder for everything Pulse keeps in Downloads: Download/Pulse. The old Pulse backup and PulseAI folders are moved into it (Backup, AI), YTXTube downloads go to Download/Pulse/YTXTube (an old YTXTube Downloads folder that is empty is removed, one with files stays), and the update APK is downloaded by Pulse into Download/Pulse/Updates (the Pulse-x.apk files loose in Downloads are moved there).
- The Video player no longer lists the camera's temporary recordings (temp_2024…).
- YTXTube playback speed: the speeds are one row (0.25 at the left end, 2.5 at the right end; it scrolls on a narrow screen), the slider gives any speed such as 1.17 (the video follows it as it moves), and Remember is a small button at the top right instead of a whole row.
- YTXTube video bar: a tap goes to that place at once and a drag follows the finger (it moved relative to where the video was before).
- Keyboard bar: the words you wrote weigh more than the language's own list, and with nothing typed the next words come from what you wrote after the last two words, then after the last one, then the words you write most, before the language's common pairs.
- Keyboard: a blocked suggestion stays gone. It could still come back through the words written last, the words a sentence begins with, a correction found by the neural model or the typo memory, or a tap on a slot that had not been redrawn; all of those are closed. (The touch model that reads a letter as the key beside it from where the finger landed, with each key's drift learned per person, was already there.)
- Keyboard colour light: it is half as fast now (one turn of the colours in 14 seconds, was 7), with a speed slider (25 to 300 %), and a new mode, Chasing light: a bright arc runs round the edge of every key. Around the keyboard and Around every key stay.
- YTXTube scrolling: while a list scrolls (and for a moment after) the glass surfaces (the bar, headers, sheets) draw a plain frosted fill instead of the blur and lens shader, which was what made fast scrolling lag.
- YTXTube video page: the list of more videos under a video was empty when YouTube answered with its newer list format (lockupViewModel); that format is read now, and a search by the title's first words follows when everything else gives nothing.
- YTXTube mini player: one tap opens the player (it showed its buttons first and opened on a second tap), and its play and close buttons stay up so close answers the first tap.
- YTXTube: pulling the video down follows the finger and goes to the mini player only after a real pull (40 % of the way, or a fast fling after at least 12 %); a small flick no longer snaps it away, and it glides into place.
- New APKs beside Pulse in the release: **PulseWatch.apk**, a Wear OS app made for round screens (crown scrolling, swipe pages, 16 apps: stopwatch, timer, world clock, pomodoro, heart rate, steps, breathe, compass, battery, calculator, notes, counter, dice, metronome, flashlight, settings), and **GlassLayer-OneUI.apk**, the One UI edition of the Glass Layer LSPosed module (its own package; balanced frame rate by default, a slow idle rate, half-size capture, per-app switches for Settings, the installers, My Files and Clock, and an inspector that writes down One UI's screens so its own classes can be hooked). Both are built separately from Pulse; a failure of either does not hold the Pulse APKs back.
